correctness.rationale: For any q>=1, the q-round EF invariant on J(n,2) preserves a partial bijection of at most 2q ground points when both n,m>=2q. For n<2q, choosing s=n+1, witnesses with <=q existential quantifiers separate all larger ground sets: for s=3,4 two-variable patterns; for 5<=s<=q a star clique of size s-1; for q<s<=2q a disjoint union of c=s-q induced paths on q line-graph vertices requiring exactly q+c distinct ground points. The root-size lemma is justified using the intersection graph structure, not inferred from computations. The resulting floor(n/2)+1 adjacent distinguishing rank and 2q-1 class count follow algebraically. A separate finite script replays q=1..4.

value.rationale: The natural classic triangular/Johnson family receives a complete sharp rank-by-rank finite-model-theoretic classification rather than a finite experimental slice: exact cutoff 2q, 2q-1 equivalence classes, all pairwise distinguishing ranks, and collapse of full FO rank q to existential rank q on the family. The key structural lemma translates induced unions of paths into minimal ground-set sizes, giving explicit witnessing formulas. This is a precise invariant with direct use as a visibility benchmark for FO logic on highly symmetric graphs, not a mere reformulation of automorphism groups or a routine isolated arithmetic constant.
